chunks: As for whatever is in it from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, I have narrated it from my father, and from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan—may Allah be pleased with them both—from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, al-Ḥimyarī, Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār, and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, all together from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār; and he is Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ṣahbān.

key_terms.جَمِيعًا: all together; indicating combined transmission from multiple teachers
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; indicating the author’s direct reporting pathway
key_terms.عَنْ أَبِي: from my father; part of the author’s sanad/isnad
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي الصَّهْبَانِ: the identifying name of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain for Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad for reports transmitted from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh. It identifies the author’s transmission route through several teachers and specifies that Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār is Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ṣahbān.
